**Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States and has about 1,100 staff. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on its German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**What the Briefing covers for the Client**

The Briefing maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to these three use cases. It frames them as expectations to verify with counsel rather than legal advice. This includes transparency expectations for the chatbot and questions about how the visual inspection pilot may be classified. United States requirements appear only as a general landscape item. The readiness discussion is anchored to the Client's piloting maturity and to establishing an AI system inventory.

The operating model overview uses the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the board-layer reference. All three rest on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

We will discuss how the intended ISO/IEC 42001 work could relate to the Client's ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001 and internal audit arrangements. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval. Implementation priorities will respect two stated constraints. Customer data must stay in the EU, and the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

**Logistics and price**

The Briefing runs for two hours, live virtual, at US$3,000. It is designed for executive leadership and board-level attendees. The audience roles are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

**What you receive afterward**

You will receive a written follow-up memo. It summarizes the decisions surfaced and our readiness observations. It also sets out three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option with a proposed timeline.

**Next step**

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a short intake call to confirm:

1. The Briefing date and attendees.
2. Whether the chatbot processes personal data.
3. The current scope of the visual inspection pilot.
4. The ISO/IEC 42001 start date, which is not yet fixed.

Kind regards,

AI Governance Academy
